title: -Ydelambdafy:inline rejects a valid lambda whose body has an existentially quantified local class type
oracle: the same program compiles and runs with the default -Ydelambdafy:method (baseline run of the existing test run/existentials3-new, which fails to compile under -Ydelambdafy:inline)
generator: wave4/harness/seeds (Driver.scala, configuration delam): run/existentials3-new and run/existentials3-old re-compiled with -Ydelambdafy:inline
detail: A method whose result type is inferred as an existential over local classes (a local trait A, an abstract class K extending A, a trait C extending K, returning (null: C), so the type is C forSome { type C <: AnyRef with A; type A <: AnyRef }) compiles, and so does a lambda () => f returning it. Under -Ydelambdafy:inline the lambda is expanded in UnCurry into an anonymous class extending AbstractFunction0[C] with Serializable, typed against the expected existential function type, and the typer reports 'type mismatch; found AbstractFunction0[C] with Serializable, required () => C forSome {...}'. The error is raised by a typer run inside the uncurry phase, so the source is accepted by the front end and rejected afterwards, with a position on the lambda. It needs a class between the trait and the leaf (without K it compiles). Ordinary code rarely returns such local types from a lambda, and -Ydelambdafy:inline is a legacy option, but it is what the existing test run/existentials3 exercises in other configurations.
fix_sketch: Type the expanded anonymous class against the erased or skolemised function type instead of the existential pt, or skip the conformance check for the expansion. No compatibility cost.
prior: none found (FO1, FT3 and PV5 are other delambdafy:inline defects; PR search for delambdafy inline existential found nothing)
